matches.rationale: No finding captures the exact cherry-picking of the FID range (2.38–2.64) while omitting poor performance at higher replacement ratios. Pred 1 mentions a different FID range (2.15–2.38) and a different inconsistency.

No finding addresses the undefined regression loss L_reg, ambiguous conditioning variable c, or inconsistency with the text's claim of using L1/L2/Huber. None of the findings relate to this method-logic issue.

No finding reports missing hyperparameter details (e.g., unspecified clip norm type, unclear warmup schedule, ambiguity about batch size definitions) in Table C.1. The existing findings about learning rate or iteration count are different discrepancies.

No finding addresses the overstated claim that grafting 'proves' utility in both short- and long-context settings. Overstatements in other sections (e.g., pred 12) are in different locations and make different claims.

The ground truth criticizes the use of '✗' without actual FID values and ambiguous ΔFLOPs definitions. Finding 7 mentions a textual contradiction about FID thresholds but does not target the omission of underlying values or the FLOP measurement ambiguity.

Finding 13 identifies the same fabricated attribution for the plant grafting reference [4] in the footnote, stating that the paper does not discuss neural network architectures. The ground truth error is about misusing a horticultural reference as inspiration for a computational method; both capture this fabricated relevance.

The ground truth error is about flawed interpretation of the band-k locality metric (averaging across all positions being misleading). Finding 6 reports a different issue: a numerical contradiction between the text and Figure 2 caption about the number of layers exceeding a threshold.

No finding points out the unfair GenEval comparison due to unspecified sampling steps or LoRA usage. Finding 8 deals with a speedup arithmetic inconsistency, which is unrelated to the experimental design protocol.

The ground truth highlights a misleading comparison of a 712M-param grafted model to a 340M-param baseline while claiming superiority. No finding addresses this parameter count discrepancy; the A.R. inconsistency (pred 11) and overclaim (pred 10) are different issues.

The ground truth says the conclusion omits limitations (e.g., full replacement failure, PixArt-Σ artifacts) and presents an overly optimistic view that grafting is lightweight. Finding 12 describes a different, more extreme overclaim ('completely solves the problem' / 'universally outperforms') not present in the given changed conclusion text.

No finding criticizes the latency measurement at an unusually small batch size (batch size=2) or the lack of throughput/utilization data. Finding 8 addresses a numerical speedup miscalculation, not the experimental design concern about batch size selection.

The ground truth points out a subtle inconsistency between the abstract's '<2% pretraining compute' and the fact that the best results use 20% data (see Figure 4(a)), which still falls under 2% but implies a selective framing. No finding catches this compute-framing issue.

No finding reports promotional language ('revolutionary,' 'paradigm shift,' 'unprecedented') in the Introduction. The overstatement findings in other sections (pred 12) are different in both location and wording.

The ground truth describes an incorrect FLOP formula in the appendix and an inconsistency between reported ΔFLOPs_op percentages and actual FLOP calculations. No finding mentions FLOP formulas or operator-level arithmetic errors.

Finding 14 correctly identifies that Reference [52] (Progressive Network Grafting for Few-Shot Knowledge Distillation) is misrepresented as relevant prior work on activation distillation for diffusion model operator replacement. The ground truth explains that the paper is about few-shot image classification, not architectural editing; both identify this misattribution.
